steps.description:
Create a python class named Circle with the following attributes:

Class Variables valid stores the number of positive entry invalid stores the number of negative entry

Object Variable radius stores the radius in float

Functions display_radius() display radius display_valid() display valid and invalid

and invalid

Write a program to create a list of circles by doing the following: 1. Ask the user to input the radius of a circle. 2. Create an object from the class and initialise its variable. Automatically update valid and invalid. 3. Append the object to a list. 4. Repeat step (1) to (3) until user enters 0 for the radius. 5. Call display__radius() function of all the objects. 6. Call display_valid() function of any one object.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Test Input

10.5 -3 6 12 0

10.5 -3 -12 0.5 0


Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input radius of a circle: 10.5 Input radius of a circle: -3 Input radius of a circle: 6 Input radius of a circle: 12 Input radius of a circle: 0 radius 10.5 radius -3 radius 6 radius 12 valid 3 invalid 1

Example 2 Input radius of a circle: 10.5 Input radius of a circle: -3 Input radius of a circle: 6 Input radius of a circle: -12 Input radius of a circle: 0.5 Input radius of a circle: 1 Input radius of a circle: 0 radius 10.5 radius -3 radius 6 radius -12 radius 0.5 radius 1 valid 4 invalid 2

Create a python class named Circle with the following attributes:

Class Variable valid stores the number of positive entry invalid stores the number of negative entry

Object Variable radius stores the radius in float

Functions area() return area of the circle rounded to 1 decimal place circumference() return circumference of the circle rounded to 1 decimal place display_info() if radius is positive, call area() and circumference() and display results display_valid() display valid and invalid

Write a program to create a list of circles by doing the following: 1. Ask the user to input the radius of a circle. 2. Create an object from the class and initialise its variable. Automatically update valid and invalid. 3. Append the object to a list. 4. Repeat step (1) to (3) until user enters 0 for the radius. 5. Call display_info() function of all the objects. 6. Call display_valid() function of any one object.

Follow the test output display format and comment your codes.

Hint: Extract the information that you need from the codes below import math radius = 5 area = math.pi * radius * radius circumference = 2 * math.pi * radius

Test Input

10.5 -3 6 12 0

10.5 -3 6 -12 0.5 1 0

Test Output (Red Text - User Input)

Test your program with the examples below:

Example 1 Input radius of a circle: 10.5 Input radius of a circle: -3 Input radius of a circle: 6 Input radius of a circle: 12 Input radius of a circle: 0 area 346.4 circumference 66.0 area 113.1 circumference 37.7 area 452.4 circumference 75.4 valid 3 invalid 1

Example 2 Input radius of a circle: 10.5 Input radius of a circle: -3 Input radius of a circle: 6 Input radius of a circle: -12 Input radius of a circle: 0.5 Input radius of a circle: 1 Input radius of a circle: 0 area 346.4 circumference 66.0 area 113.1 circumference 37.7 area 0.8 circumference 3.1 area 3.1 circumference 6.3 valid 4 invalid 2
